title: The Stolen Chime Array
logline: A cultural curator hires an armed pilot to recover a bronze ceremonial chime array stolen by a smuggler right before the Centennial Founding Festival, before security destroys the pirate hull.

roles.description: The station cultural preservationist; proud, fussy, frantic that the century-old bronze bells will be melted into scrap.
An opportunistic black-market salvager holding the chimes in a stripped blockade runner.
A light combat raider fitted with oversized cargo grapples and illegal military thruster overburners.
The heavy-handed station defense militia, eager to execute pirates on live holiday broadcasts.
A reinforced display pavilion on the station concourse designed to showcase founding historical relics.
An unmonitored docking pylon in the outer debris ring used by black-market fuel traders.

public_situation: The Centennial Founding Festival is twelve hours away, but the historic orbital chime array has vanished from {role:curator_vault}.
private_truth: {role:festival_curator} staged the theft with {role:fence_corsair} to claim municipal insurance, but the smuggler doubled the ransom demand.

beats.public_change: {role:civic_guard} puts the station on general combat alert, threatening to open fire on any vessel departing the perimeter berth.

missions.reason: He needs certified industrial alloy bars purchased from exchange docks and brought to the perimeter berth as the down payment on the ransom.
missions.private_fact: He diverted the museum's annual endowment fund to purchase the alloy without logging it in the municipal audit.

beats.public_change: The smuggler demands a secondary handover code, deploying automated escort drones to ward off approaching patrol ships.

missions.reason: He needs the patrol picket attacking the perimeter dock destroyed before their stray railgun slugs rupture the chime crates.
missions.private_fact: The civic guard captain is his ex-brother-in-law, who suspects the curator is running a personal embezzlement scheme.

beats.public_change: {role:raider_cutter} breaks moorings and heads for the system jump gate with the chime array lashed to its dorsal hull.

missions.reason: He needs the raider's sublight engines crippled before the pirate jumps out of system with the sacred bells.
missions.private_fact: The corsair hails mid-fight offering to split the bronze chimes into raw foundry ingot bars and share thirty percent of the scrap payout.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot disables the raider and returns the chime array to the pavilion.
resolutions.summary: The bronze chimes sound on time across {system}. {role:fence_corsair} is imprisoned, and {role:festival_curator} conceals his role in the original heist.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot shot the engines off a pirate cutter to save the station's founding bells in time for opening ceremonies.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot accepts the corsair's deal and lets the raider jump out.
resolutions.summary: {role:fence_corsair} escapes with the antique chimes. {role:festival_curator} is arrested when the audit discovers the empty vault, and the festival opens in silence.

consequences.public_summary: Dockside lore claims a mercenary helped a smuggler scrap the colony's sacred bronze bells for black-market copper.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot fails the combat contracts or the ransom exchange falls apart.
resolutions.summary: Militia fire shatters the cargo cradle in open space. The founding bells are pulverized into orbital shrapnel, ruining the festival.

loose_threads.detail: The shipping crate contains an unsigned insurance payout rider dated two days before the chime array was reported stolen.
A commercial scrap furnace on the rim posted a purchase order for ancient bell-grade bronze twelve hours before the vault alarm sounded.
The transponder code on {role:raider_cutter} displays a decommissioned civic guard serial number registered to the curator's brother-in-law.

radio_hooks: Station authorities announce reward for information regarding missing founding chimes.
Centennial preparations continue under heavy armed security deployment.
Black market chatter spikes around antique high-tin bronze scrap ingots.

voice_direction.festival_curator: Flustered, high-pitched, and incessantly wiping sweat from his brow. Speaks of antique metallurgy with religious fervor while desperately trying to conceal his balance sheet.
voice_direction.fence_corsair: Gravelly, sarcastic, and completely unimpressed by historical heritage. Treats sacred century-old bells like generic copper ore awaiting a smelting torch.

title: The Procession Beacon
logline: A cantor organizing an annual orbital lantern parade discovers navigation guide buoys have been deliberately skewed, threatening to steer hundreds of pilgrim shuttles into asteroid shears.

roles.description: Guides the ceremonial flight patterns of civilian pilgrim ships; devout, cautious, struggling with whether ritual is worth civilian lives.
Station flight safety auditor; secular, impatient, eager for an excuse to cancel the un-taxed religious gathering.
Hundreds of independent mining families who pilot their shuttle craft in close orbital formation for annual blessings.
A radical ideological faction determined to engineer an accident to prove modern navigational automation is cursed.
An ancient domed temple station perched over the system's primary asteroid ring.
An automated navigational beacon mooring that marks the turning point of the ceremonial orbital run.
The central observation hub where municipal officials and families gather to watch the illuminated formation.

public_situation: Shuttle pilots across {system} mount amber illumination beacons for the annual Pilgrimage of Lanterns around {role:lantern_sanctuary}.
private_truth: {role:traditionalist_league} re-angled the optical lenses at {role:parade_waypoint} so the procession's lead ships will drift directly into rock shears.

beats.public_change: Pilgrim vessels assemble in loose formation while {role:port_inspector} warns telemetry drift will result in flight bans.

missions.reason: He needs certified high-precision optical collimator lenses brought from station optics shops to replace fogged beacon mirrors before the parade launches.
missions.private_fact: He suspects his own deacon assisted the saboteurs to protest the introduction of automated formation computers.

beats.public_change: Telemetry alarms chime as test drones following the optical guide path drift three kilometers into unmapped rock spurs.

missions.reason: He needs an independent ship to scan the waypoint array and pinpoint exactly which prism alignment has been falsified.
missions.private_fact: The cantor is privately terrified that his entire lifetime of navigational scripture is mathematically flawed.

beats.public_change: {role:port_inspector} issues an official decree revoking the parade charter unless manual ground-truth charts are produced.

missions.reason: He needs the sealed historical ledger containing the manual triangulation coordinates retrieved from the temple sanctuary crypt.
missions.private_fact: The temple ledger contains marginal notes showing that a previous procession disaster thirty years ago was also blamed on divine will.

beats.public_change: The pilgrim fleet begins engine warm-ups outside the airlocks, refusing to disembark despite conflicting beacon readings.

missions.reason: He needs the verified triangulation slate delivered to the inspector before hotheaded pilgrim captains trigger an unguided mass launch.
missions.private_fact: {role:traditionalist_league} representatives are offering to endorse the cantor as high patriarch if he buries the proof of sabotage.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds the proof of sabotage and the manual correction tables. The crowd waits on the flight line.

options.label: Deliver the corrected coordinates to guide the fleet safely
Support the inspector's complete cancellation of the flight
Let the cantor quietly adjust the formation without exposing the saboteurs

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot delivers the true coordinates and exposes the tampering.
resolutions.summary: The pilgrim fleet completes their illuminated flight along true coordinates. {role:traditionalist_league} is exposed, and {role:procession_cantor} preserves the holy tradition.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot uncovered sabotaged navigation buoys and guided five hundred lantern ships through the asteroid shoals.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot allows the cantor to quietly correct the mirrors without arresting the league.
resolutions.summary: The procession flies safely along corrected mirrors, but the sabotage is hidden. {role:traditionalist_league} retains their influence, and the cantor lives in quiet shame.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot fails the mission runs or backs the safety shutdown.
resolutions.summary: The lantern procession is officially grounded. Bitter rioting breaks out across the berths, and {role:pilgrim_congregation} accuses the port authority of religious persecution.

loose_threads.detail: The replacement collimator crate bears customs shipping stencils invoiced to an ideological printing press three jumps away.
The temple sanctuary's auxiliary oxygen line is encumbered by a debt contract held by a corporate director aligned with the league.
The safety certificate on {role:parade_waypoint} was stamped with the seal of an inspector who died during the previous eclipse season.

radio_hooks: Lantern procession pilots tune thruster radios across {system} in preparation for evening launch.
Port inspection office warns of severe navigational hazards along the ceremonial route.
Temple council dismisses safety warnings as administrative interference with sacred rites.

voice_direction.procession_cantor: Soft-spoken, melodic, and burdened by immense responsibility. Speaks with rhythmic poetic cadences that falter into strained pauses when calculating debris velocities.
voice_direction.port_inspector: Abrasive, blunt, and dismissive of ceremonial tradition. Speaks in clipped operational terminology, treating hundred-year-old prayers as air traffic control violations.
